sources.title: Kabam: Improvements to Liquid Courage and Double Edge Masteries
Community discussion: Help with masteries please
Community discussion: Best mastery setup for Battlegrounds

coreMasteries.name: Parry
coreMasteries.points: 1 minimum; add more when stun duration matters
coreMasteries.why: Unlocks the basic Parry play pattern. Extra ranks are mainly about stronger/longer stun utility rather than unlocking the mechanic itself.

coreMasteries.name: Dexterity
coreMasteries.points: 1 point for the essential evade utility
coreMasteries.why: One of the most important universal movement tools. Additional ranks are usually lower priority than unlocking other high-value masteries.

coreMasteries.name: Precision
coreMasteries.why: Reliable critical-rate value across a broad roster. Community setups consistently prioritize the full Precision node over bridge points.

coreMasteries.name: Cruelty
coreMasteries.why: Broad critical-damage value and a common high-priority offensive investment.

coreMasteries.name: Block Proficiency
coreMasteries.why: Reduces chip from blocked hits and Parry-heavy play, which matters in questing, war and difficult boss content.

coreMasteries.name: Willpower
coreMasteries.why: Provides sustain while non-damaging or damaging debuffs are active. It becomes much more important in Recoil/Liquid Courage/Double Edge setups.

coreMasteries.name: Recovery
coreMasteries.why: Improves healing received and pairs naturally with Willpower-heavy sustain builds.

coreMasteries.name: Glass Cannon
coreMasteries.why: Efficient attack increase at the cost of health. Strong for players comfortable trading durability for damage.

coreMasteries.name: Despair
coreMasteries.points: 1-3 when your roster applies many debuffs
coreMasteries.why: Adds heal-control value to debuff-heavy attackers and is often useful in regeneration matchups.

coreMasteries.name: Deep Wounds
coreMasteries.points: Invest when Bleed attackers are a major part of your roster
coreMasteries.why: Strongly benefits Bleed-centric champions but gives much less value to rosters that rarely rely on Bleed.

coreMasteries.name: Assassin
coreMasteries.points: 1-5 depending on available points and goals
coreMasteries.why: Improves finishing power when the opponent is low on health. This can matter in timed fights such as Battlegrounds.

coreMasteries.name: Mystic Dispersion
coreMasteries.points: Invest when Mystics are a major part of your offense/defense
coreMasteries.why: Excellent for Mystic-heavy rosters that regularly interact with opponent buffs, but not universally valuable.

presets.title: General / Non-Recoil Setup
presets.summary: A flexible setup for questing, story progression and mixed rosters without the self-damage of the Recoil branch.
bestFor: Players who do not want Recoil damage
priorities: Start with Parry and Dexterity, then build toward Precision, Cruelty and Block Proficiency.
Use Willpower and Recovery when you value sustain, especially if your common fights place debuffs on you.
Spend remaining points according to roster: Deep Wounds for Bleed teams, Mystic Dispersion for Mystic-heavy rosters, Despair for debuff-heavy attackers, Assassin for faster finishes.
Treat bridge masteries as unlock costs first; do not assume more points in every early node are better than reaching stronger end-of-branch options.
watch: There is no universal best all-around build: roster, progression and content matter.
Glass Cannon trades health for damage, so do not max it automatically if you rely on durability.
Deep Wounds and Mystic Dispersion are poor investments when your roster rarely uses the mechanic they support.

presets.title: Battlegrounds Setup
presets.summary: A health-score-aware approach that values fast finishes on attack and annoying defensive masteries without automatically sacrificing health to Recoil.
priorities: Use a non-Recoil baseline by default unless a specific meta or roster clearly benefits from Liquid Courage / Double Edge.
Keep Precision and Cruelty strong on offense; Assassin can be valuable because finishing the final portion of a fight faster can improve time score.
Despair is valuable when your attackers stack debuffs into healing defenders.
Defensive options such as Limber, Stand Your Ground and Inequity/Resonate can add friction to opponent fights; prioritize them only if your BG defense benefits from them.
Mystic Dispersion is a strong specialist choice when your deck is Mystic-heavy and repeatedly fights buff-heavy attackers.
watch: Recoil, Double Edge and Liquid Courage can reduce remaining-health score or punish Special-heavy attackers, so they are not the default recommendation for BG.
Masteries should match the current season meta; a node package can change the value of a normally strong choice.
Saved Battleground mastery loadouts can preserve a dedicated BG setup even when your normal questing masteries later change.

presets.title: Recoil / Liquid Courage / Double Edge
presets.summary: A high-damage setup built around Recoil, Liquid Courage and Double Edge. It can be excellent for compatible rosters but is not a universal upgrade.
bestFor: Champions that tolerate or benefit from Bleed/Poison
priorities: Use the minimum Recoil investment required to access the branch, then commit to Liquid Courage / Double Edge only if your roster can handle the self-debuffs.
Willpower becomes a major support mastery because it can recover health while debuffs are active; Recovery can further improve sustain.
Coagulate can reduce the impact of the opening Bleed from Double Edge for champions that are not fully Bleed immune.
Prefer champions that are Bleed/Poison immune, resistant, shrug the effects, or otherwise turn the self-debuffs into an advantage.
watch: Recoil damages you after Special Attacks, which can be a serious problem for champions whose rotations depend on repeated Specials.
Liquid Courage and Double Edge apply self-damaging debuffs; roster compatibility matters more than the headline attack increase.

Kabam changed Liquid Courage and Double Edge attacker damage scaling in 2024 so the self-damage uses the lesser of modified or base Health. That helps boosted attackers but does not remove the tradeoff.
This setup is usually less attractive for long-form content and many Battlegrounds decks where health preservation matters.

presets.title: Specialist Masteries
presets.summary: How to choose between Mystic Dispersion, Deep Wounds, Despair, Assassin and defensive branches once your universal core is in place.
priorities: Mystic Dispersion: prioritize when Mystics form a large part of your active roster and frequently interact with opponent buffs.
Deep Wounds: prioritize when a significant share of your best attackers rely on Bleed duration for damage.
Despair: prioritize for debuff-heavy attackers and heal-control matchups.
Assassin: prioritize when faster final-phase damage is valuable, especially in timed fights.
Limber / Stand Your Ground / Inequity-style defense: consider when Battlegrounds or Alliance War defense matters more than general questing efficiency.
watch: Do not max every specialist mastery at once; each one has an opportunity cost.
A specialist mastery can be excellent for one roster and almost wasted for another.
Revisit these choices when your main roster, BG deck or Alliance War role changes.
